option_analysis.summary: Use Python http.server and unittest with no external dependency.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Lower UI realism but gives deterministic real HTTP evidence without stack setup noise.

option_analysis.summary: Introduce a frontend framework and browser-app build pipeline.
option_analysis.tradeoff: More product-like UI but adds dependencies unrelated to the pilot validation target.

option_analysis.summary: Keep submissions in memory behind a threading.Lock.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Matches local workflow continuity while avoiding unnecessary storage setup.

option_analysis.summary: Introduce a durable database or file-backed queue.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Adds persistence but increases migration and cleanup work outside the pilot goal.

option_analysis.summary: Generate opaque thanks-page ids with secrets.token_urlsafe.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Avoids leaking user input and keeps ids unpredictable with minimal code.

option_analysis.summary: Use sequential, timestamp, or input-derived thanks-page ids.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Easier to inspect but leaks ordering or user-derived information.

option_analysis.summary: Escape submitted name and message on server-side rendering.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Keeps the rendered thanks page safe even when client validation is bypassed.

option_analysis.summary: Rely on client-side validation or raw template interpolation.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Less server code but leaves XSS risk in the generated response.

option_analysis.summary: Use real HTTP requests in tests against the running server boundary.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Costs a little setup time but proves the route, cookie, and rendering path together.

option_analysis.summary: Test handlers directly with unit-only calls.
option_analysis.tradeoff: Faster tests but misses wiring, HTTP semantics, and browser-facing behavior.

interfaces.contract_summary: POST /feedback validates required fields, stores valid submissions, and redirects to /thanks?id={id}.

input_params.name: message
input_params.validation: must be non-blank after trimming and fit the form size limit

output_params.name: thanks_redirect
output_params.description: Redirect to /thanks?id={opaque_id} after a valid submission is stored.

error_codes.condition: name or message is blank, malformed, or exceeds the accepted form size

boundary_behaviors.scenario: blank, oversized, malformed, and valid feedback submissions
boundary_behaviors.expected_behavior: invalid submissions return the documented error path without persistence; valid submissions are stored once and redirect to a thanks id

interfaces.contract_summary: GET /thanks?id={id} renders escaped feedback content for known ids and a readable not-found page for unknown ids.

input_params.name: id
input_params.validation: must match a stored opaque feedback id
input_params.description: Opaque thanks-page id returned after successful feedback submission.

output_params.name: thanks_page_html
output_params.description: Escaped feedback name and message for a known id; readable not-found response for missing or unknown ids.

error_codes.condition: id is missing or does not match a stored feedback submission

boundary_behaviors.scenario: known, missing, and unknown feedback id lookup
boundary_behaviors.expected_behavior: known ids render escaped feedback content; missing or unknown ids render a readable controlled response without leaking stored records

data_architecture.summary: Valid feedback submissions are stored in an in-memory dictionary behind a threading lock; no durable storage or external datasource is introduced.
storage_decisions: Use process-local in-memory storage because the pilot validates standard-chain flow, not persistence.
data_flows: POST /feedback validates form data, stores escaped-source values under an opaque id, and redirects to GET /thanks?id={id}
data_architecture.consistency_strategy: A threading.Lock guards submission storage during local ThreadingHTTPServer tests.

cross_cutting_concerns.decision: No authentication is required for the feedback pilot; anonymous form submission is intentional.
Blank fields, malformed Content-Length, oversized bodies, missing ids, and unknown ids return readable errors.
Invalid submissions keep default HTTP access-log observability.
The app introduces no external configuration; runtime remains standard-library only.
